One sweep with every part, both readers and the probes shows the around route forming layer by layer and turns Fig 6's "after the data" readings into the rule-based readings (a)-(d). decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch47.yaml, 47.8; per model, the rest descriptive). l_J = the first layer from which the lookup's extra loss without J++ stays <= 0.10; l_P = the first layer where the position share under the whole change is >= 0.20; l_probe = the first layer where the slot probe is >= 0.80. (a) Handoff: l_P >= l_J, report l_P - l_J (Q35.1's failure on the 27B predicts a gap of about 4 layers there). (b) The address forms before it is used: l_probe <= l_P on every model; if the probe reaches 0.80 only after l_P, say so. (c) Identity leaves the lens: identity share with only-J++ >= 0.5 at the earliest interpretable layer and <= 0.1 by L, while identity with only-I_l rises to >= 0.3 by L, on >= 2 of 3 models; report the crossing layer. (d) Never the value, at any depth: value <= 0.05 at every interpretable layer. (e) The recall side: the layer window where the whole change switches the recall >= 0.5, and whether without-J++ costs it >= 0.3 throughout that window (the recall's own onset layer reported beside l_J). 'Not interpretable' where the whole change switches < 30% of a reader. As computed (fixed by the agent before any run; Dan may override before the run): Scenes: x6_routes' generator (seed 2510; locker-first), conditions C2 and C0, X0's gate (0.80 per reader on unedited scenes) and eligibility; the eligible C2 scenes split by bridge entity (seed 0; entities in a seeded order fill the test half to N_TEST scenes, the rest form the fit half, >= 150 or the run stops). title: Batch 51.2 on Qwen3.5-9B (L12): joint head ablation under the address swap. 49.7's items and swap 2 (mu_k - mu_j) at the bridge word; every recorded attention head ranked by its attention move on the fit half; on the read half the top k in {1, 3, 5, 10}, all heads of the best layer, each mean-ablated at the last token and at the question tokens under the swap; matched random sets of k heads from the same layers (5 draws); SEALED until Q51.2
command: export BJ_TARGET=qwen3.5-9b BJ_DEVICE_MAP=; uv run python scripts/x51_heads.py run --name qwen35_9b_x51_2 --why "batch 51, test 51.2 (jobs/c3/batch51.yaml; Q51.2): 49.7's items and swap at L12; heads ranked by their last-token attention move on the fit half (49.7's stored attention); top 1/3/5/10, the best layer, matched random sets mean-ablated at the last / question tokens on the read half; sealed"
question: Under the address swap, do a few heads whose attention follows the written address carry the switch together (ablating them jointly undoes it), or is the dereference spread over many heads?
why_it_matters: 49.7 found heads whose last-token attention moves to the written slot's sentence (moves > 1) but zeroing the single best head left the switch unchanged on all three models. Joint ablation separates redundancy among a few heads (a small set) from a distributed read (even the whole best layer cuts < 0.3); on the 9B and 27B three of four layers are Gated DeltaNet, which no head ablation here touches.

hypotheses.Q51.2: Dan's answer in predictions/2026-10-28_dan.md (Q51.2, per model: (a) a small set (k <= 10) / (b) distributed / (c) neither); not committed when this spec was written, so the run is sealed: no verdict in the job (scripts/x51_heads.py verdict and view refuse until the Dan: line is committed).

decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch51.yaml, 51.2, Dan 28 Oct 17:10). Read half; decisive site the last token (49.7's decisive site), the question tokens beside under the same rules; cluster bootstrap over bridge entities (10,000, seed 0); EPS 1e-9 at the bars. switch = the read-half swap pairs' share where the lookup answers slot k's locker (the swapped-in slot); cut = (switch - switch under the ablation) / switch, both read in this run. "A small set carries the dereference": some top-k set, k in {1, 3, 5, 10}, cuts >= 0.5 while the identity answers (read pairs answering slot j's locker under the swap; share whose lookup answer changes under the ablation) move <= 0.10 and the recall's answer moves <= 0.10 (swap + ablation vs swap), and the random sets of k heads from the same layers cut <= 0.15 (mean over the draws). "Distributed": every head of the best layer together cuts < 0.3. Label: small set if it holds, else distributed if it holds, else neither; both flags reported. CPU beside (verdict stage): per read pair, the summed attention move at the last token (every recorded head; the top 10 beside) vs switched, from 49.7's stored forward; logistic fit (on the standardised sum, slope also per unit) and AUC with its cluster-bootstrap interval. Report beside: per set and site the switch with and without the ablation, the cut with its interval, identity / recall changed, the clean answers lost (none + ablation vs none, both readers), the random draws' cut mean, SD, min and max. As computed (fixed before any run; Dan may override): items = 49.7's (x8_write.eligible: the routes test's C2 scenes, O, gate 0.80 per reader, the first 300; the run asserts they are 49.7's run's items in order and the same fit / read halves by bridge entity, random.Random(0)); heads = those 49.7 recorded (every softmax-attention layer > L; Gated DeltaNet layers skipped and logged); ranking = every recorded head by its mean attention move at the last token on the fit half's switched swap pairs (no fit pair switched: every fit swap pair), read from 49.7's stored attention.npz and outcomes (no rerun of 49.7; move = (mass on slot k's sentence - mass on slot j's) under the swap minus the same under none), ties lower layer then head; the one ranking (last-token move) serves both ablation sites; top k is taken across layers, so 'the top 10 across layers' is the k = 10 set (one arm, not two); best layer = the layer of the rank-1 head (49.7's best-layer convention); random control per top-k set = the same number of heads in each of its layers, drawn from that layer's other heads (top-ranked heads of the same layer are not excluded), 5 draws; for the best-layer set (no head left in that layer) 5 draws of its size from the other recorded layers; random.Random(512), drawn in a fixed order; mean ablation = the head's slice of o_proj's input (its attention output after the gate, head_dim wide) replaced at the site's positions by its mean over the fit half's unedited prompts of the same reader at the same position: the last (read) token; the question tokens by index within the question (8 lookup / 9 recall tokens, fixed per reader, asserted); each reader ablated at its own positions (the recall's prompt is one token longer; 49.7 had zeroed the recall at the lookup's positions); every batch row (none and both swaps) ablated; reads = X0's batched chat read (one batch of 3 rows per reader, set and site), a no-ablation baseline read beside; classes as x8_write (target = slot k's digit, original = slot j's, third, other); the switched label for the CPU-beside fit is 49.7's (the forward that recorded the attention).

the best-layer set: 5 random sets of its size from the other recorded layers (beside; no head is left in the layer)
heads ranked on the fit half (49.7's stored attention), every ablation read on the other half (split by bridge entity, seed 0)

command: export BJ_TARGET=qwen3.5-9b BJ_DEVICE_MAP=; uv run python scripts/x51_jread.py run --name qwen35_9b_x51_10 --why "Batch 51, test 51.10 (jobs/c3/batch51.yaml addendum_2; Q51.10): read / write per position and reader at 15 layers (every 2nd layer L2-L30); main-test items of the qwen3.5-9b X0 run, write and remove arms on 49.1's locker-first items; sealed"
question: Does the bridge entity (the intermediate) pass through J-space where the second hop is made -- at the question's pick token and at the last token -- for the lookup (in-context: entity -> its locker) and the recall (parametric: entity -> fact)? Read: is it readable through his top-10 lens directions there before the answer forms; write: does his J-part swap or the J++ part of the change move the answer as the whole state does?
why_it_matters: Neel: it is strange that the intermediate does not go through J-space. Our 'the lookup is blind to the J++ part' is a statement about the bridge token; the workspace paper's claim and the latent two-hop literature (Yang et al. 2024; Biran et al. 2024) put the bridge entity at the last token in the middle layers. Either the lookup's intermediate passes through J-space at the question even though the bridge word's identity does not, or the in-context hop routes around the lens end to end: the direct answer to the comment.
